grid.note: stored dB COGs; change = post_db - pre_db

hv_flood_rule.rule: post_db < -23 dB AND post_db - pre_db < -3.0 dB AND pre_db >= -23 dB AND not pre-event water
hv_flood_rule.threshold_source: 5th percentile of the post-scene HV dB histogram (-22.65 dB -> -23 dB); HV lacks a bimodal water mode, so the water-dark tail is the scene's darkest ~5 %. For comparison the HH-mask adaptive_threshold (tiled Otsu, clamped <= -22.0 dB) gives -22.00 dB (adaptive) — the clamp is what makes that estimator usable on cross-pol.

sensitivity.note: candidate_km2 (post-MMU) if threshold were N dB looser

agreement.note: HH candidates = cog/wa_2025_flood_nisar_20251210.tif reprojected nearest onto the 60 m grid

double_bounce.landcover_source: MCD12Q1.061 LC_Type1 2024 (IGBP) via GEE — 061/2025 product is empty over the AOI in Earth Engine, nearest year used

interpretation: HH pixels brightening >= +3 dB (Dec 4 -> Dec 16) cover ~109 km2, but only ~2 % sit within 500 m of the darkening flood candidates and their land cover is dominated by 'other' classes (~76 % — shrub/grass/snow/barren) with forest ~22 %, cropland <1 % and urban ~1 % — so the bulk of the brightening is probably NOT flood-adjacent double-bounce; widespread wetting (soil/canopy moisture rise, freeze-thaw or snow-state change) or BETA calibration drift between passes are at least as likely. The small flood-adjacent bright fraction remains consistent with inundated-vegetation/urban double bounce. In HV, inside the HH candidates the post median is about -21.3 dB (vs -16.6 dB in HH) with a -4.7 dB median drop, but a strict HV < -23 dB + drop >= 3 dB rule maps only ~0.05 km2 with zero overlap (IoU 0.0): cross-pol water darkening does not reach that tail inside the mapped candidates, so at 60 m and BETA calibration both masks stay candidates, not confirmed inundation.
